newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Foreign trade in May ended with a deficit of 11.2 billion crowns. The trade deficit since the beginning of the year reached 64.6 billion crowns, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau.
- The crown yesterday climbed to a record high since the cancellation of the fluctuation band. It reached 18.475 to the mark.

- While the Czech Statistical Bureau expects GDP growth this year to slow to two to three percent, Patria Finance predicts no growth, Expandia predicts one percent growth, and the Finance Ministry says growth will be under two percent.
- The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development is organising a seminar on business problems during transformation on June 25 and 26 in Prague. About 29 countries should be represented.

- During the first five months of this year, the leading Czech manufacturer of vertical lathes, Toshulin, exported machines worth 119 million crowns, 26 percent to Germany, 13 to the United States 10.4 to Belgium and 9.7 to Switzerland.
- Until the beginning of June, Vitkovice had gross profits of 28 million crowns.
- For the first five months of this year, Tatra Koprivnice had gross profits of 29 million crowns.
- Cizovicka Cementarna will obtain a 100 percent share in Austrian Zementwerk Kirchbichl after increasing its basic capital by 285 million crowns by issuing new shares.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The cabinet will give Zetor Brno a helping hand only when the Industry and Trade Ministry adds a privatisation project to its proposal for reviving this leading tractor maker.

- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka will decrease interest rates today for seven-day and two-week timed accounts, but it will increase interest rates on all other deposits, except six-month and nine-month.

- Nearly 60 companies yesterday established the Defence Industry Association, whose members include CKD Praha, Ceska Zbrojovka, Chemapol, Let Kunovice, Synthesia Pardubice, Omnipol, Praga, Sellier & Bellot, Skoda Plzen, Tatra Koprivnice and Adamovske Strojirny.

- Although experts agree that commercial and investment activities of banks should be more separated, opinions differ on how deep this cut should be. The proposal from the Civic Democratic Alliance to change banks to either commercial or investment banks before their privatisation has little support.

- The Health Ministry released another 300 million crowns of the one-billion-crown state loan for General Faculty Hospital in order to protect Minister Jan Strasky's promise that half its debts to drug distributors would be paid by the middle of the year.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The director of public insurer Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna strictly informed doctors that the value of the points they receive for operations will not increase to one crown from July 1, because there is no money with which to do this.
- Chairmen of coalition parties decided yesterday on their priorities, which are reforms of the social security system, privatisation of the National Property Fund and speeding up court hearings.

- As part of the 14th international NATO conference for military and political planning, which is being held in Prague, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said the Czech Republic will ensure transformation of its army and will provide the necessary funding for this.

- A spokesman of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), Jaroslav Orel, yesterday said that he would not rule out that certain members of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) would be interested in changing to KDU-CSL, because its programme coincides with modern political trends.

PRAVO - The Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) supports the proposal from Christian Democratic (KDU-CSL) leader Josef Lux for cuts in the social sector to finish at the end of 1998, but ODA conditions it on fundamental reforms. The leader of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, is against time restrictions.

- Czech Agriculture Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux met with his Polish counterpart in Warsaaw yesterday and signed two intercabinet agreements for cooperation in veterinary and botanical fields, which coincide with EU regulations.
- According to IVVM, the current government is preferred to the government before last November's Senate elections by 26 percent of Czechs, while 25 percent prefer the old regime.

- According to the first official results of the peoplemeters used to measure Czech television watching, Nova television was watched in the first week of June by 54 percent of citizens above 15 years of age, CT1 by 27 percent, Prima by eight and CT2 by six percent.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
